name: Reactor Coolant Pump
notes: US EPR FSAR Ch 5.4-derived. No US EPR built; all numeric params are estimates (approx:true). RCPs are non-Class-1E loads: no EDG backup, flywheel coastdown on LOOP. Component-level granularity per decision 2026-07-03. Electrical chain (switchyard/NAT/buses) modeled here temporarily - tagged migrateTo:EPSS. Per-RCP electrical group (master BUS-52 -> RCP-BUS -> FDR-52 motor / MCC-52 aux branch) is a deliberate sim design, not AREVA practice - decided 2026-07-03. MCC has dual feed via break-before-make ATS: normal from RCP-BUS, alternate from non-1E SBO-diesel-backed 480V bus; SSS solenoid on battery 125VDC (SBO-proof) - decided 2026-07-03.

devices.name: 400kV switchyard (grid source)
devices.behavior: Grid connection. Deenergized = loss of offsite power (LOOP): all downstream normal buses drop, RCPs coast down on flywheels.

devices.name: Normal auxiliary transformer {t}
devices.behavior: Steps switchyard voltage down to normal MV buses. NAT-1 feeds NBUS-1, NAT-2 feeds NBUS-2. Fault deenergizes its bus.

devices.name: 13.8kV normal (non-1E) bus {t}
devices.behavior: Each normal bus feeds two RCP electrical groups (1&2 on NBUS-1, 3&4 on NBUS-2). Energized iff upstream NAT in-service and switchyard energized. NOT backed by EDGs.

devices.name: SBO diesel generator {t} (non-1E)
devices.behavior: Non-Class-1E station blackout diesel. Auto-starts on loss of voltage on its SBO bus; picks up the bus in ~30s. NOT one of the four Class 1E EDGs - those feed safety divisions only.

devices.name: SBO bus {t} normal feeder breaker (SBO-BUS-{t}-52)
devices.behavior: LV (480V) main breaker, downstream of SBO-BUS-{t}-XFMR. Normally closed; trips on bus/load faults. NOTE: faults inside the transformer itself are upstream of this breaker and clear at NBUS-{t} feeder protection (simplified - no MV-side breaker modeled).

devices.name: SBO bus {t} step-down transformer (SBO-BUS-{t}-XFMR)
devices.behavior: 13.8kV -> 480V transformer on the SBO bus normal (grid) feed path.

devices.name: 480V SBO-backed bus {t} (non-1E)
devices.behavior: Diesel-backed non-safety 480V distribution/instrumentation bus. Normally grid-fed: NBUS-{t} -> SBO-BUS-{t}-XFMR -> SBO-BUS-{t}-52 (LV main); diesels stay in standby. On loss of normal supply SBO-DG-{t} auto-starts and re-energizes it (~30s). Grid/generator transfer device (SBO-BUS-{t}-ATS) and DG output breaker (SBO-DG-{t}-52) NOT YET MODELED - decided to defer 2026-07-03. Alternate feed source for RCP MCCs (1&2 from SBO-BUS-1, 3&4 from SBO-BUS-2).

devices.name: SBO bus tie breaker (SBO-BT-52)
devices.behavior: Normally-open tie between SBO-BUS-1 and SBO-BUS-2. Close supervised by SBO-BT-25 interlock: dead-bus close (one side deenergized - single DG then carries both buses, watch DG capacity) or live-parallel close only when in sync. With both DGs running and tie closed, diesels share load on droop.

devices.name: SBO tie sync-check relay (SBO-BT-25)
devices.behavior: Supervises SBO-BT-52 closing. Compares voltage, frequency and phase angle across the open tie. 'dead-bus-ok' when either side is deenergized (close freely). 'in-sync' when both sides live and matched (V within ~5%, slip < ~0.1Hz, angle < ~10deg) - operator trims DG governor to achieve this. 'blocked' otherwise - close command physically inhibited (out-of-phase closing wrecks both machines).

devices.name: RCP {n} master group breaker (RCP{n}-BUS-52)
devices.behavior: Master breaker for the whole RCP {n} electrical group: feeds RCP{n}-BUS, from which both the motor (via FDR-52) and all auxiliaries (via MCC-52) derive. Tripping it kills everything RCP {n} - motor AND aux power (OLP, lube, SSS solenoid). No MCR control: local operation + BUS-86 lockout trip only. Normally stays closed; routine motor start/stop uses FDR-52.

devices.name: RCP {n} group bus (RCP{n}-BUS)
devices.behavior: Per-RCP 13.8kV bus downstream of RCP{n}-BUS-52. Two taps: RCP{n}-FDR-52 (motor) and RCP{n}-MCC-52 (auxiliaries). Energized iff RCP{n}-BUS-52 closed and NBUS-{bus} energized.

devices.name: RCP {n} group bus incomer CTs (RCP{n}-BUS-CT-A)
devices.behavior: CT set immediately downstream of RCP{n}-BUS-52: measures total current entering the RCP {n} group bus. Feeds the 87B differential (incomer leg) and the 51 backup overcurrent in RCP{n}-BUS-PROT.

devices.name: RCP {n} bus differential CTs, motor end (RCP{n}-BUS-CT-B1)
devices.behavior: CT set at the RCP end of the motor feeder (motor terminal box): closes the 87B zone on the motor branch. Inside containment - signal exits via shared instrument EPA. NOTE: placing this at the motor end (not at FDR-52) puts the feeder cable inside the BUS differential zone, overlapping the motor 87 zone (CT-A to CT-B) - a feeder fault picks up BOTH differentials and trips the master too.

devices.name: RCP {n} bus differential CTs, MCC tap (RCP{n}-BUS-CT-B2)
devices.behavior: CT set on the MCC branch immediately upstream of RCP{n}-MCC-XFMR primary: closes the 87B zone on the auxiliary branch. Current 'lost' between BUS-CT-A and (B1 + B2) = fault inside the group zone.

devices.name: RCP {n} bus protection package (RCP{n}-BUS-87B/-51)
devices.behavior: 87B bus differential (loss detection): compares BUS-CT-A against BUS-CT-B1 + BUS-CT-B2; mismatch beyond tolerance = current lost inside the group zone (bus, feeder cable, MCC tap up to XFMR primary) -> instantaneous pickup. Plus 51 time-delayed backup overcurrent from BUS-CT-A: picks up when fault current persists because a downstream breaker (FDR-52 or MCC-52) failed to clear. Either element latches RCP{n}-BUS-86. 51 delay coordinates above downstream relays (selectivity); 87B is instantaneous - see BUS-CT-B1 note on zone overlap with the motor 87.

devices.name: RCP {n} master lockout relay (RCP{n}-BUS-86)
devices.behavior: Latches on RCP{n}-BUS-PROT pickup; trips and holds RCP{n}-BUS-52 open (whole group dead). Manual local reset only, after fault investigation.

devices.name: RCP {n} motor breaker (RCP{n}-FDR-52)
devices.behavior: Connects RCP motor to RCP{n}-BUS via feeder RCP{n}-FDR. The operational breaker: MCR control switch start/stop drives this one. Close blocked unless start permissive satisfied and RCP{n}-86 reset. Trip commands: MCR stop, RCP{n}-86 (electrical faults), SI trip, seal-cooling-loss trip. 'tripped' requires operator reset to 'open' before reclose.

devices.name: RCP {n} feeder current transformers, breaker end (RCP{n}-CT-A)
devices.behavior: CT set clamped on RCP{n}-FDR at the FDR-52 output. Secondaries fan out to: 87 differential (bus-side leg), 50/51 overcurrent, MCR ammeter. Does not interrupt the line.

devices.name: RCP {n} feeder current transformers, motor star point (RCP{n}-CT-B)
devices.behavior: CT set at the motor star point, inside containment. Closes the 87 differential zone (everything between CT-A and CT-B is the protected zone: cable, terminal box, stator). Signal exits via shared instrument electrical penetration assembly (EPA).

devices.name: RCP {n} group bus voltage transformer (RCP{n}-VT)
devices.behavior: VT on RCP{n}-BUS. Feeds the 27 undervoltage element, the start-permissive voltage check, and bus voltage indication.

devices.name: RCP {n} motor protection relay package (RCP{n}-87/-50/-51/-27)
devices.behavior: Differential (87: compares CT-A vs CT-B), instantaneous/time overcurrent (50/51: from CT-A), undervoltage (27: from RCP{n}-VT on the group bus). Pickup drives RCP{n}-86 to lockout. Protects the motor zone; trips land on FDR-52 only.

devices.name: RCP {n} motor lockout relay (RCP{n}-86)
devices.behavior: Latches on any motor protection pickup; trips and holds RCP{n}-FDR-52 open. Manual local reset only, and only after protection targets cleared. Non-electrical trips (MCR stop, SI, seal-cooling-loss) bypass the 86 and act on the FDR-52 trip coil directly - restart after those needs no local reset.

devices.name: RCP {n} auxiliary feeder breaker (RCP{n}-MCC-52)
devices.behavior: LV (480V) main breaker on the MCC normal feed path, downstream of RCP{n}-MCC-XFMR; output lands on the ATS normal input. Normally closed at all times (auxiliaries must live while the motor is stopped: pre-start OLP run, coastdown jacking oil). Tripped by RCP{n}-MCC-PROT on MCC-branch faults. NOTE: faults inside MCC-XFMR are upstream of this breaker - they clear at RCP{n}-BUS level (BUS-PROT backup -> BUS-86 -> BUS-52 master trip; ATS then transfers auxiliaries to alternate).

devices.name: RCP {n} MCC step-down transformer (RCP{n}-MCC-XFMR)
devices.behavior: Small 13.8kV -> 480V transformer on the NORMAL feed path, directly off RCP{n}-BUS; output feeds RCP{n}-MCC-52 (LV main). Fault here clears upstream at RCP{n}-BUS level (no MV-side breaker modeled); the ATS transfers auxiliaries to alternate.

devices.name: RCP {n} MCC alternate feeder breaker (RCP{n}-MCC-ALT-52)
devices.behavior: Feeds the ATS alternate input from SBO-BUS-{sbo} (already 480V - no transformer needed). Normally OPEN; closed automatically by the RCP{n}-MCC-ATS transfer logic as part of a fast switchover, reopened on manual re-transfer to normal. Own overcurrent protection trips it on faults in the alternate path.

devices.name: RCP {n} MCC automatic transfer switch (RCP{n}-MCC-ATS)
devices.behavior: 2-position break-before-make transfer switch with mechanical interlock - physically cannot parallel the two sources. Normal input: RCP{n}-MCC-XFMR (from RCP{n}-BUS). Alternate input: RCP{n}-MCC-ALT-52 (from SBO-BUS-{sbo}). FAST auto-transfer on loss of normal input: closes MCC-ALT-52 and swings to alternate within transferDelayS (~a few cycles) - quick enough that MCC contactors hold in and loads never see the outage, provided SBO-BUS-{sbo} is live. Covers group-local losses (master trip, BUS fault, MCC-XFMR fault) seamlessly; on LOOP the SBO bus is dead too until SBO-DG picks it up (~30s), so the MCC still sees that outage. Re-transfer back to normal is MANUAL (local), reopens MCC-ALT-52. Not a breaker: cannot interrupt fault current - the upstream 52s do that.

devices.name: RCP {n} motor control center (RCP{n}-MCC)
devices.behavior: 480V LV bus for all RCP {n} auxiliaries: oil lift pump, lube oil equipment, machine instrumentation power (SSS solenoid moved to battery 125VDC). Energized iff ATS on a live input: (normal: MCC-52 closed + MCC-XFMR in-service + RCP{n}-BUS energized) OR (alternate: MCC-ALT-52 closed + SBO-BUS-{sbo} energized). Losing it while running: pump keeps running, but no jacking oil for next stop/start - its own casualty.

devices.name: RCP {n} MCC protection package (RCP{n}-MCC-50/-51/-50G/-27)
devices.behavior: 50/51 overcurrent + 50G ground fault at the LV main: faults on the MCC bus or its loads -> trip RCP{n}-MCC-52 (NOT the master - selectivity; master's BUS-51 backs this up if it fails to clear). MCC-XFMR internal faults are outside this zone (upstream of the LV main) and clear at RCP{n}-BUS level. 27 LV undervoltage: no trip - fires AUX POWER LOSS annunciator and blocks motor start permissive.

devices.name: RCP {n} motor + flywheel
devices.behavior: Single-speed induction motor, vertical shaft, integral flywheel. FDR-52 closed -> starting (high inrush ~5x FLA, accel ~15s) -> running at sync slip. FDR-52 opens -> coasting: flywheel gives slow coastdown (several minutes to standstill) maintaining core flow during the critical first seconds.

devices.name: RCP {n} oil lift pump
devices.behavior: High-pressure jacking oil pump, powered from RCP{n}-MCC (NOT from behind FDR-52 - must run before motor start and during coastdown). Must run before motor start (lifts shaft off thrust bearing) and during low-speed coastdown. Auto-started by start sequence, auto-stopped above speed threshold, auto-restarted on coastdown below threshold. Starting the motor without lift pressure damages the thrust bearing. Cannot run if MCC deenergized.

devices.name: RCP {n} lube oil system
devices.behavior: Self-contained bearing lube oil with CCWS-cooled oil coolers; support equipment powered from RCP{n}-MCC. Loss of CCWS -> oil temp rises -> bearing temps rise -> alarm, eventually bearing damage if pump kept running. 'failed' with motor running damages bearings over minutes.

devices.name: RCP {n} shaft seal stage {s}
devices.behavior: Three-stage controlled-leakage shaft seal. #1 takes nearly full RCS dP; #2 and #3 are staged backups. Degradation raises stage leakoff and shifts dP to next stage. All three failed with pump at pressure = seal LOCA unless SSS closes. Seal cooling from CVCS injection or thermal barrier; loss of BOTH while at pressure degrades seals over ~10-30 min.

devices.name: RCP {n} standstill seal
devices.behavior: N2-actuated metal-to-metal seal; actuation solenoid powered from battery-backed 125VDC (SBO-proof by design: stored N2 does the work, battery only fires the solenoid). Closes ONLY at standstill (shaft below ~10 rpm); closing on a rotating shaft destroys it. Auto-closes on seal-failure signal at standstill; also MCR-actuated. Stops seal LOCA from a stopped pump with failed seals. Requires N2 accumulator pressure AND DC control power.

devices.name: RCP {n} thermal barrier HX
devices.behavior: CCWS-cooled coil between RCS and seal package. Backup seal cooling: if CVCS seal injection is lost, thermal barrier alone keeps seals within temperature limits. Cooling iff CCWS flow available (CCWS containment isolation closes it off).

devices.name: RCP {n} hydraulic section (impeller/diffuser)
devices.behavior: Converts shaft speed to loop flow (flow ~ speed for sim purposes; head-flow curve later). 'damaged' (e.g. debris, cavitation) reduces delivered flow at rated speed.

signals.name: RCP {n} seal trouble (derived)
signals.expr: RCP{n}-LEAKOFF-FLOW > 8 OR RCP{n}-SEAL-TEMP > 90 OR any(RCP{n}-SEAL{s} != ok)

permissives.expr: RCP{n}-OLP == running AND RCP{n}-OLP-PRESS > 100 AND RCP{n}-SEALCOOL-OK AND RCP{n}-BUS-VOLTS > 12.4 AND RCP{n}-AUXPWR-OK AND RCP{n}-86 == reset AND RCS-PRESS > 25
permissives.notes: BUS-VOLTS > 12.4 implies master 52 closed and NBUS energized. AUXPWR-OK (MCC alive) required because OLP and instrumentation run from it. RCS-PRESS min for seal dP is a startup-procedure value, approx. Oil lift pre-run time enforced by start sequence, not this permissive.
Dead-bus: one DG feeds both buses (verify DG capacity vs combined load - overload stalls/trips it). Live-parallel: manual sync by governor trim. Never closable out-of-phase.
Closing on rotating shaft destroys the SSS - sim should enforce and model violation damage. Solenoid on battery DC - works in full SBO.

autoActions.notes: ECCS actuation trips all four RCP motors (LOCA: prevents pumping the break; small-break: preserves loop seal). Master 52 and MCC stay closed - auxiliaries keep running for coastdown. Signal owned by future ESFAS file.
Motor electrical protection path: PROT picked-up -> 86 lockout -> FDR-52 trip, reclose blocked until local 86 reset.
MCC-branch faults (50/51, 50G) clear at the MCC feeder breaker - NOT the master (selectivity). The 27 LV-UV element alarms and blocks start but never trips.
87B differential (instantaneous, current lost inside the group zone) or 51 backup (downstream breaker failed to clear).
Whole group dead: motor AND auxiliaries. Local BUS-86 reset required.

autoActions.expr: ATS normal input dead sustained 0.1s AND RCP{n}-MCC-ATS == normal
autoActions.notes: Fast break-before-make auto-transfer to SBO-BUS-{sbo}: seamless for MCC loads (contactors hold in) when the SBO bus is live - covers BUS-52 master trips, group bus faults, MCC-XFMR faults. On LOOP the SBO bus is dead too until SBO-DG picks it up (~30s gap - OLP restarts when the bus returns). Re-transfer to normal is manual/local only and reopens MCC-ALT-52.
Loss of both seal injection AND thermal barrier cooling: procedure requires trip; sim auto-backs-up the operator after delay. Delay approx.

autoActions.expr: RCP{n}-SEAL-TROUBLE AND RCP{n}-SPEED < 10 AND N2-SUPPLY-OK AND DC-OK
autoActions.notes: Auto standstill-seal closure on seal failure at standstill.

autoActions.expr: RCP{n}-AUXPWR-OK AND RCP{n}-SPEED < 100 AND (start sequence active OR RCP{n}-MOTOR == coasting)
autoActions.notes: Jacking oil below cutoff speed; off above it. Needs MCC power.

steps: start RCP{n}-OLP, wait prestartRunMinM (2 min) with OLP-PRESS > 100 bar
close RCP{n}-FDR-52 -> motor 'starting', inrush ~5x FLA for accelTimeS
at sync speed motor 'running'; loop flow ramps to rated

diesel backup; picks up bus ~30s after loss of normal. Transfer device + DG output breaker deferred - direct link for now

HP jacking oil to thrust bearing
closed lube circuit to upper/lower bearings
thermal barrier coil; lost on CCWS containment isolation
seal injection enters between THB and SEAL1

shaft annulus opens into pump casing / RCS

#2/#3 leakoff to reactor coolant drain tank
suction from crossover leg (SG {loop} outlet) - see rcs/loop.json

87B motor-branch leg; exits containment via instrument EPA
delayed backup pickup latches master lockout
trip + hold master open - whole group dead
pre-start run; also auto during coastdown < 100 rpm

STOP position = direct trip (bypasses 86 - no local reset needed after normal stop)
